title: H2O: Heavy-Hitter Oracle for Efficient Generative Inference of Large Language Models
one_line_claim: A KV-cache eviction policy that retains heavy-hitter tokens identified by accumulated attention scores, achieving 5-10x cache reduction while maintaining comparable accuracy.
method_summary: H2O tracks accumulated attention scores for each token during inference. At each generation step, it greedily selects top-k heavy-hitter tokens by cumulative attention weight, evicting all others from the KV-cache while keeping the current token. Yields compression ratios up to 95% sparsity in practice.

key_findings.finding: H2O with 20% heavy hitters achieves up to 29x throughput improvement over DeepSpeed Zero-Inference and Hugging Face Accelerate on OPT-6.7B, and 3x over FlexGen on OPT-30B.
key_findings.quote: H2O with 20% heavy hitters improves the throughput over three leading inference systems DeepSpeed Zero-Inference, Hugging Face Accelerate, and FlexGen by up to 29x, 29x, and 3x on OPT-6.7B and OPT-30B

key_findings.finding: Attention distributions exhibit extreme sparsity: over 95% of attention weights go to fewer than 5% of tokens (heavy-hitters).
key_findings.quote: We observe that the attention distribution in LLMs is sparse: more than 95% of the attention is paid to fewer than 5% of the tokens at each attention head in most layers.

key_findings.finding: H2O maintains comparable or superior accuracy to dense-cache baselines while achieving 5-10x KV-cache memory reduction.
key_findings.quote: H2O achieves comparable performance to the dense baseline while reducing the KV-cache memory usage by 5-10x

relation_to_herald.shared: Both target KV-cache compression in generative LLM inference, operate at token granularity during generation, and evaluate on standard benchmarks (OPT, LLaMA).
differs_on: H2O uses attention-based heuristics to select which tokens to evict; HERALD predicts when compression causes catastrophic failures before they occur.
H2O is a deterministic compression policy; HERALD is a probabilistic hazard detector with a configurable horizon parameter.
H2O aims to maximize throughput/memory; HERALD aims to forecast non-termination, looping, and instruction amnesia.
